faqs.a: UTM parameters are five short query tags (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content) that you add to a URL. Analytics tools read them to tell you exactly which link, email or ad brought each visitor.

All five exist, but only three are required for clean reports: utm_source (where the traffic comes from), utm_medium (the channel, e.g. email or cpc) and utm_campaign (the campaign name). utm_term and utm_content are optional extras.
Keep one naming convention and stick to it: lowercase, underscores instead of spaces, e.g. summer_sale. Mixing Summer-Sale, summer sale and SUMMER_SALE creates three separate rows in your reports.
faqs.q: How should I name my campaigns?

faqs.a: utm_source names the referrer (newsletter, facebook, google). utm_medium names the channel (email, social, cpc, referral). Example: source=newsletter, medium=email for a link in your email newsletter.
faqs.q: What is the difference between utm_source and utm_medium?

faqs.q: Can I add UTM tags to a URL that already has parameters?

faqs.a: No. UTM tags only label the visit for your own analytics; they do not change what the visitor sees, and they do not affect search rankings.

utm-builder.formula:
final URL = base URL + "?" + "utm_source=" + source + "&utm_medium=" + medium + "&utm_campaign=" + campaign [+ "&utm_term=" + term] [+ "&utm_content=" + content]
Values are percent-encoded. If the base URL already has a query string, new parameters are appended with "&".
howTo: Paste your destination page URL into the Website URL field.
Type the utm_source: where the visitor comes from (e.g. newsletter, facebook).
Type the utm_medium: the channel (e.g. email, social, cpc).
Type the utm_campaign: the campaign name (e.g. summer_sale).
Optionally add utm_term (paid keyword) and utm_content (to tell two links apart).
Copy the finished URL and use it in your email, ad or social post.
keyFacts: UTM stands for Urchin Tracking Module, from the Urchin analytics software Google acquired in 2005; the naming lives on in Google Analytics.
The five standard parameters are utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term and utm_content.
utm_source identifies the referrer, utm_medium the marketing channel, and utm_campaign the specific promotion.
utm_term records the paid-search keyword, and utm_content distinguishes links that point to the same URL (e.g. two buttons in one email).
Analytics platforms read UTM tags automatically; visitors never see anything different on the page.
Special characters in values are percent-encoded, so spaces and symbols never break the link.

limitations: UTM tags only track visitors after they click; they cannot track impressions or offline reach.
They describe your own analytics only: typos in values (Sumr_Sale) still work but pollute your reports.
Do not put UTM tags on internal site links: they overwrite the original traffic source in your reports.
Very long URLs with all five parameters can look messy when shared raw; consider a shortener for social posts.

utm-builder.workedExample:
Website URL: https://example.com/summer-sale
utm_source = newsletter, utm_medium = email, utm_campaign = july_promo
Step 1: start with the base URL. Step 2: append "?" and the first tag: utm_source=newsletter. Step 3: join the rest with "&": utm_medium=email, then utm_campaign=july_promo.
Result: https://example.com/summer-sale?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=july_promo
That link is 94 characters long and tells analytics: traffic came from the newsletter, through email, for the July promo campaign.
